lead: Organic growing begins with a useful bit of housekeeping: keep as much plant material as possible in the garden, turn it into compost and return it to the soil.

blocks.title: Look after the ground
blocks.text: Use mature compost to improve the soil and replenish what crops take from it. Organic soil needs to breathe, so avoid compaction: keep feet and barrow wheels on the paths. Respect the life under your feet: don't light fires on the soil, and don't poison the ground with chemicals that you wouldn't be prepared to eat yourself.

blocks.title: Work with the place you have
blocks.text: A plant in the right soil, with correct levels of sunshine and water, will almost always succeed. Grow the crops and varieties that suit your ground - you will find this out with time and experience; every site and every plot is different. Keep a record of successes as well as failures; work with Nature to grow what is right for your garden and your garden will ultimately flourish.

blocks.title: Deal with the cause
blocks.text: Look closely before reaching for a remedy. Check moisture, roots and recent weather. Hand-pick damaging pests where practical and fit suitable crop protection: know the likely arrival times of pests in your area and net vulnerable plants before the pests arrive.
